findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
findings.description:
Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection each start a goroutine that derives its context from the request context (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` at lines 51, 110, 135, 163). The Go HTTP server calls `w.cancelCtx()` right after `ServeHTTP` returns (`net/http/server.go:2073-2075`), so that context is cancelled as soon as the response is sent. The playlist legacy store passes `ctx` straight into its service and DB calls (`pkg/registry/apis/playlist/legacy_storage.go:115`, `:142`, `:160`, `:171`). A cancelled context makes those calls fail, so the legacy copy is silently dropped on a timing-dependent basis. The only trace is a histogram label, because the errors are not logged (see the swallowed-errors finding below).

Before this diff the legacy write was synchronous, so the regression is introduced here. Mode 1 uses the same pattern (`dualwriter_mode1.go:54`, `:92`, `:126`, `:159`, `:193`, `:225`) and should be fixed there as well.

Suggested fix: `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...)`. `WithoutCancel` is available in Go 1.21+, and both `go.mod` (1.22.4) and `pkg/apiserver/go.mod` (1.21.10) support it. It keeps context values such as the namespace info that `legacy_storage.go:102` reads.

findings.title: Delete no longer tolerates NotFound from storage, so legacy is never cleaned up
findings.description: The removed code treated a storage NotFound as non-fatal and still deleted from legacy. The new code returns immediately on any storage error, so legacy is skipped. Scenario: storage delete succeeds, the async legacy delete fails silently, and the user retries. The retry gets NotFound from storage and never reaches legacy, leaving an orphaned row. Mode 1 reads from legacy (`dualwriter_mode1.go:84`), so that playlist would reappear if the mode were switched. The DeleteCollection error path has the same change (lines 154-158; the original continued to legacy on storage error).

findings.title: Update hands legacy the raw `objInfo`, so legacy re-runs the transform against its own object
findings.description: The removed code passed `updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}`, so legacy persisted the object storage had already computed. The new code passes `objInfo`. The legacy store then calls `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` against its own copy (`legacy_storage.go:142-147`). If the update is patch-style, the result depends on the old object, so the two stores can diverge, which is the situation mode 3 is meant to surface. Re-invoking an `UpdatedObjectInfo` after the storage layer has consumed it is also not guaranteed to be safe (I did not verify the k8s patcher on this point).

findings.title: Errors from async legacy writes are discarded without logging
findings.description: The goroutines record only a boolean error label and never log. The same applies at lines 112-113, 139-140, and 165-166. The original code logged each of these errors. This matters concretely: the playlist legacy `DeleteCollection` always returns an error (`legacy_storage.go:191-192`), so every mode 3 DeleteCollection now diverges with no log line at all.

findings.title: Metrics are recorded against the wrong histogram on several paths
findings.description: Storage failures are recorded with `recordLegacyDuration` in Create (line 45) and Update (line 129). The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with `recordStorageDuration` (line 166). Per-store latency and error rates are therefore mixed up.

findings.title: `name` is passed as the `kind` label on Delete success
findings.description: The metric label set is `{is_error, mode, kind, method}` (`metrics.go:23`). Line 106 passes `name`, while the error path at line 103 passes `options.Kind`. Every object name then creates a new Prometheus series, which is unbounded cardinality. Mode 1 has the same bug at `dualwriter_mode1.go:155`, but this diff introduces it into mode 3.

findings.title: Mode 3 is unreachable from configuration
findings.description: `SetDualWritingMode` only transitions 1→2 and 2→1 (lines 198-218), and the function ends with a `#TODO` (line 220). A fresh KV store defaults to Mode1 (line 190), and the function returns `currentMode` (line 222). The caller (`pkg/services/apiserver/builder/helper.go:169-184`) therefore gets Mode1 for a desired mode of 3. `TestSetDualWritingMode` (`dualwriter_test.go:18-63`) covers only modes 1 and 2. Mode 3 can only be reached by constructing `NewDualWriter` directly, as the unit tests do. If the gating is intentionally staged, the PR should say so.

findings.title: The new "mode 3" integration subtests actually run mode 1
findings.description: The subtests at lines 132, 191, and 287 pass `DualWriterDesiredModes: Mode3`, but per the previous finding they run in mode 1. They pass without exercising mode 3 at all. Once mode 3 is actually active, the existing "Check playlist CRUD in legacy API appears in k8s apis" assertions (around lines 371-449) may no longer hold, because k8s reads would come from storage. I did not verify whether the legacy-API write path reaches storage, so this is unverified.

findings.title: Shared mock makes legacy and storage expectations interchangeable, and the legacy path is never verified
findings.description: `ls` and `us` share one `*mock.Mock` (lines 53-54), so an expectation registered for legacy also satisfies a storage call. In the error case (lines 37-44) no storage expectation is set. The storage failure is matched by the legacy expectation at line 41, so the test passes without ever reaching the legacy path. No test calls `AssertExpectations`, and the async legacy calls are never awaited. The core mode 3 behavior, the legacy write, is therefore untested. Delete's NotFound behavior has no test either. Mode 1's tests use the same pattern (pre-existing), so this is codebase-wide, but this file copies it.

findings.title: Delete builds a per-request `log` but puts `d.Log` into the context
findings.description: Create, Get, List, Update, and DeleteCollection all put `log` into the context. Delete puts `d.Log`, so name, kind, and method are dropped from downstream log lines.

findings.title: Get logs NotFound at error level
findings.description: Every 404 on a GET logs an error. Mode 2 treats NotFound as an expected case (`dualwriter_mode2.go:83-90`).

findings.title: Request objects are shared with goroutines without a copy
findings.description: `obj` is passed to the legacy goroutine directly. Mode 1 deep-copies first (`dualwriter_mode1.go:51`). I found no legacy code that mutates `obj`, so this is a latent race rather than a live one.

findings.title: Test hygiene issues in dualwriter_mode3_test.go
findings.description:
- Line 145 names the List case "error when listing ... is not implemented", but it tests a storage error.
- Line 74 has reversed `assert.Equal` arguments (expected and actual are swapped).
- Line 119 shadows the package-level `p` that every other test in the file uses.
- The `assert.NotEqual(t, obj, anotherObj)` assertions are vacuous.

findings.title: One `go.work.sum` checksum does not match the module's replace directive
findings.description: The added `github.com/grafana/prometheus-alertmanager v0.25.1-0.20240422…` entry is not the version `go.mod:482` replaces to (`…20240625…`), so it may be stale. The `grafana-azure-sdk-go/v2` entries do match a requirement in `go.mod:87`. I could not run `go mod verify` or `go mod tidy` because Bash is disabled.

findings.title: Removing the local registry in TestMode1_Get compiles and is behavior-neutral
findings.description: Package-level `var p = prometheus.NewRegistry()` is declared at `dualwriter_mode1_test.go:27`, so the `prometheus` import is still used and `p` resolves.
